text: Since 3.18.0 we added a retry around reservation persistence. Tests cover one retry; I'll add a connection lifecycle test.
The new retry should be safe; success path closes the connection. Let's watch the dashboards.
Active connections are trending up but DB CPU is only 27%. Could be a long-running query?
Checkout p95 has drifted from ~180ms to 420ms. Error rate still low. Investigating.
Campaign is a little busier after worker concurrency went up. Could this just be traffic?
Traffic is up about 8%, but active DB sessions have climbed almost 3x. Need to compare acquisition rate vs release rate.
The reconciliation index PR merged recently. Checking whether it created lock waits or a slow query.
Orders DB CPU is normal and top query duration is flat. Please don't assume the DB is overloaded from connection count alone.
TRIGGERED SEV1: checkout timeout ratio > 12%, pool pending borrowers rising.
Pool wait timeout errors now widespread. Restarting pods may clear it, but let's capture pool metrics first.
Users report checkout spinner; campaign traffic is peaking. Is gateway saturation the primary cause?
Gateway CPU rises after checkout latency. The earliest divergence is checkout pool active/idle age, not gateway CPU.
I suspect the reporting index change. It landed around the time we noticed DB sessions.
The DB is clearly maxed out; the new index probably caused it. We should roll back the database migration first.
Reporting query p95 is 180ms, same as baseline. No lock pile-up. These sessions are mostly from checkout pods.
Counter-evidence: DB CPU 31%, lock waits flat, report query p95 unchanged. Connection ages and client application_name point to checkout-service.
pg_stat_activity shows many checkout app connections with age > 30 minutes, idle in transaction; the count rises monotonically.
Looking at PR #2042: catch/retry branch can skip close(). That matches the old Jira note about testing repeated SQLTransientException.
I initially thought traffic was the cause, but the pool acquire rate is not matched by close/release events. That fits a leak.
I reviewed that PR and missed the cleanup path. This is more likely than campaign traffic or the index.
PR #2054 merged: close JDBC connection in retry failure path; connection lifecycle test passed.
checkout-service 3.18.1 rollout complete: 6/6 pods ready.
New connections are being returned normally; old leaked sessions are draining. Pool wait and p95 falling.
Resolved. Root cause: JDBC connection leak in retry exception path; follow-up for leak detection and mandatory lifecycle tests.
